worktree.rationale: The default child-thread route creates a worktree off the parent commit. An explicit existing checkout shares that folder, and non-Git projects also share the project folder. A worktree is checkout separation. Child access cannot exceed the parent, but no hostile-code container/VM boundary follows from these tools or from whole-service Docker hosting.

coordinator.rationale: Threadlines supplies parent-thread delegation tools: the current agent starts named child threads and receives their final replies, with parent/child relationships owned by the product. Agents can start threads is gated off/ask/auto by user settings. Provider readiness, plan billing and access checks apply before a child can run. thread_send provides follow-up messages to child threads; parent reports arrive asynchronously after the calling turn. With reportBack true, each child final reply returns as a message and wakes the parent, including later self-started child turns. The caller does not block or poll.

telemetry-default.rationale: The policy describes operational usage/reliability events sent to PostHog, with its content exclusions and startup-failure exception. Official builds enable usage analytics by default. The sender consults the saved usageAnalyticsEnabled preference and documented environment override. Settings can disable usage analytics. THREADLINES_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false is a documented process override; throwaway test/CI runs are separately suppressed. The easiest documented control is the in-app Settings opt-out.
